body: A gunman opened fire in the food court of Greenwood Park Mall, south of Indianapolis, on July 17, 2022, killing three people before an armed bystander shot and killed him. A woman who was shot in the leg and her family sued the mall's owner, Simon Property Group, L.P., and its security contractor, Universal Protection Service, LLC (d/b/a Allied Universal Security Services), in Marion Superior Court in 2024. According to the Court of Appeals' June 9, 2025 opinion, the amended complaint alleges the gunman walked through the parking lot and into the mall past security patrols and cameras carrying a long backpack of the kind used for rifles, spent more than an hour in a food-court restroom stall assembling weapons, and that no security personnel were in the food court when the shooting began.

Simon and Universal moved to dismiss, arguing a mall shooting is not foreseeable as a matter of law, so no duty arises. Judge Christina R. Klineman denied the motions on May 14, 2024, and the Court of Appeals affirmed on June 9, 2025. The Indiana Capital Chronicle described both courts as rejecting the dismissal bids on procedural grounds.

At the January 15, 2026 argument, according to the Capital Chronicle, the family's attorney said the victims should be able to investigate the mall's security as the gunman passed at least a dozen cameras. Simon's attorney argued that seeing someone walk into a mall with a backpack does not put anyone on notice of a mass shooting, and pointed to Indiana law allowing people to carry guns openly. Justice Christopher Goff asked whether the security contractor should take steps to recognize a potential shooter; the attorney warned against 'judicially sanctioned profiling.' Wrongful-death suits by the families of the three people killed are on hold until the court rules.

timeline.label: Gunman kills three people in the Greenwood Park Mall food court; an armed bystander shoots and kills him
The wounded woman and her family file an amended complaint against Simon Property Group and Universal Protection Service in Marion Superior Court
Trial court denies the defendants' motions to dismiss
Indiana Court of Appeals affirms the denial
Indiana Supreme Court hears oral argument
